prompt:
Create one landscape 3:2 architectural MOOD BOARD, a single polished sheet on a plain warm light background, titled "POLARTON / HILLSIDE KIT". Crisp authentic vanilla Minecraft voxel blocks and textures only; no characters, villagers, animals, modded blocks or smooth non-voxel architecture. Southern Mississippi cotton mill agricultural settlement, circa 1880–1930: simple sturdy lived-in rural buildings for cotton, tobacco and corn. Use the attached site image as terrain reference, preserving its hill climbing west, stepped grassy terraces, dark stone retaining walls, existing streets, driveways and spruce-fenced pads, lowland stream and village at the east foot. No invented flat landscape in the site view.

COMPOSITION: three whole-kit thumbnail takes across the upper/middle sheet, a clearly lettered block palette strip below, and four large signature detail callouts along the bottom. All three thumbnails depict this same EIGHT-building kit, with restrained alternate roof/massing arrangements. Thumbnail A is the authoritative long sample row, an isometric view of ALL EIGHT modules in correct left-to-right order, with fine plot boundaries and numbers 0–7; enough space to distinguish every building. Thumbnail B shows the WHOLE SET distributed on the actual supplied hillside landform and pads, stream on the low side, church on highest plateau, homes and school above, working buildings below. Thumbnail C is a closer alternate roof/massing take of the whole kit, still showing all eight, with cutaway hints for interiors. Keep thumbnail scales small enough to fit but readable; clean organized architectural board, no overlapping panels.

AUTHORITATIVE SAMPLE GRID: 96 wide, eight adjacent plots, each exactly 12 x 14. Dirt/gravel lane along x at z=0..4; plots at z=5..18; plot i x=12i..12i+11. Every sample-row module faces north toward lane, front yard z=5..8, gate x=12i+5..6. Each plot has identical spruce perimeter fence, paired two-wide spruce fence gates centered on front, lantern posts at both front corners. All roofs, porches, chimneys, yards remain inside their own plot. Site-placement thumbnail rotates each intact module to face its existing street. Church graveyard has a small INTERNAL pale picket-like vanilla fence, never replaces perimeter spruce fence.

ORDER, identity and site placement:
0 / site 1: two-storey cotton gin house, muted ochre board-and-batten, dark slate-like roof, front wagon bay, loft hay door and projecting hoist beam; clear left machine bay reserved for owner's Create gin, visibly marked floor and wall shaft opening; no invented mod machinery. Lowland, north.
1 / site 2: one-room schoolhouse, pale clapboard, small bell cupola, cloakroom porch and yard bench, cartography_table inside. Plateau, west.
2 / site 3: 1.5-storey hill farmhouse, warm wood clapboard on stone piers, deep front porch, rear kitchen ell, composter. Plateau, east.
3 / site 4: blacksmith/wheelwright, open-front forge shed, masonry chimney set into side wall, anvil and smithing_table, block-built wheel in progress and cart under lean-to. Lowland near stream, south.
4 / site 5: white clapboard settlement church, tall slender steeple visible from village, small internal graveyard and lectern by entrance. Highest plateau, east.
5 / site 6: tall narrow dark timber tobacco curing barn, vertical boards and vent gaps, hanging leaf-like vanilla vegetation tiers visible inside, base fire/flue. Southern flat, north.
6 / site 7: slatted corn crib elevated on piers, adjoining granary ramp, sacks represented by vanilla blocks, simple block-built scale. Southern flat, north.
7 / site 8: better-off gin owner's two-storey house, muted brick and cream timber, wraparound porch, projecting bay and balcony overlooking village downhill. Plateau edge, west.
Distinguish roof palettes: weathered oxidized copper tin-like roofs, deepslate slate, spruce shingles. Keep rural modest proportions, not mansion-sized.

FOUR DETAIL CALLOUTS with clear labels: 
"GIN / HOIST + SHAFT": loft hay door, wood hoist beam, wagon opening and reserved machine bay with marked shaft.
"PORCH / STEP-FREE ENTRY": deep porch eave and window, centered two-wide spruce gate, bottom-slab approach: at most three half-height advances then a level landing at least 2 long and 2 wide, final cell level before main door; ground floor no more than 1 block above yard, two-cell slab ramp; no front stairs or full-block jumps.
"HEARTH / WALLED AIR FLUE": sectional voxel detail, campfire at BOTTOM hearth with hay hidden under floor, wall-integrated exterior masonry chimney entirely within plot, enclosed 1x1 AIR flue open from fire to mouth, constant-width masonry through roof, roof ends against stack, uncrowned open mouth 1–2 courses above roof; never fire on roof or freestanding room chimney.
"FAMILY / LOFT PLAN": farmhouse or owner's house cutaway, 3–4 complete beds each head against solid wall with no window or door behind, two clear blocks above, accessible door-to-bed route; table, stove beside hearth, indoor walkable stairs whose top step meets upper floor flush. Lantern lighting throughout.

SWATCH STRIP: show actual cubic vanilla block samples grouped by role with exact fully qualified Minecraft ids lettered legibly underneath, all matching materials depicted. Walls: minecraft:stripped_spruce_log, minecraft:birch_planks, minecraft:white_concrete, minecraft:bricks. Trim: minecraft:spruce_planks, minecraft:calcite. Roof: minecraft:oxidized_cut_copper_stairs, minecraft:deepslate_tile_stairs. Windows: minecraft:glass_pane. Accents: minecraft:spruce_fence, minecraft:spruce_fence_gate, minecraft:lantern. Use two tidy lines of swatches if needed to keep full ids legible. Label small caption "8 CUT-OUT MODULES / 12 × 14 / NORTH-FACING SAMPLE ROW". Architecture and authentic Minecraft block language dominate, lettering secondary. No extraneous decorative illustrations, no photorealism, no characters or animals.
reads: Eight numbered, spruce-fenced modules form a single lane-facing row with lantern-lit gates.
The hillside view places homes, school and steepled church above the working buildings, among stone terraces overlooking the stream and village.
The ochre cotton gin has a broad wagon opening, loft hay door, hoist beam and marked machine-bay shaft.
The pale schoolhouse has a small bell cupola; the farmhouse has a deep timber porch.
The open smithy reads as a working forge through its masonry chimney, tools and sheltered work area.
The white church and tall dark steeple provide the settlement’s uphill landmark.
A tall timber tobacco barn contrasts with the airy slatted corn crib and adjoining granary.
The owner’s brick house stands out through its green copper roof, wraparound porch, projecting bay and balcony.
Four detail panels show gin equipment space, the porch approach, a sectional hearth flue and furnished family floors; some rendered entries appear stair-like despite the slab-ramp labels.
The vanilla block palette is grouped by role with Minecraft ids. The generated sheet is saved as moodboard.png.
